title: How loud nature's sounds are in decibels
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How loud is thunder in decibels?
How loud is too loud for my ears?

explain.say: Loudness is measured in decibels. Zero decibels is about the quietest sound a young person can hear, and gently rustling leaves are about 20.

draw.text: How loud nature's sounds are in decibels

explain.say: A whisper is about 30 decibels and normal talking about 60. That might look like double, but the decibel scale works in jumps.
Every 10 decibels more means the sound carries 10 times as much energy, and it seems roughly twice as loud. So 60 decibels has a thousand times the energy of 30.
Thunder close by can reach around 120 decibels, a million times the energy of normal talking. Sounds above about 85 decibels for a long time can damage hearing.

faq.a: A decibel, written dB, is a unit for measuring how loud a sound is. The scale starts near zero for the quietest sound we can hear, and each 10 decibels is ten times more sound energy.

faq.q: How loud is thunder in decibels?
faq.a: Thunder from a nearby lightning strike can reach around 120 decibels, about as loud as a rock concert right by the speakers. Far away it is much quieter.

faq.q: How loud is too loud for my ears?
faq.a: Long exposure to sounds above about 85 decibels, like heavy traffic, can slowly damage hearing. Around 120 decibels can be painful, and very loud bangs can cause damage instantly.

faq.q: Why does 10 more decibels sound twice as loud?
faq.a: The decibel scale counts in multiples. Adding 10 decibels means ten times the sound energy, which our ears hear as roughly twice as loud.
asks: How does the decibel scale work?
Is 80 decibels twice as loud as 40?

faq.q: What is the quietest sound we can hear?
faq.a: Zero decibels is set near the faintest sound a young, healthy ear can hear. Some very quiet places, like a still desert, can be under 20 decibels.

facts: Each increase of 10 decibels means ten times the sound intensity and sounds roughly twice as loud.
Long exposure to sounds above about 85 decibels can damage hearing.

quiz.say: A sound goes from 60 decibels to 70 decibels. How much more sound energy is there?
quiz.why: Every 10 decibels up is ten times the sound intensity.

wrong.0: The decibel scale is not a simple add-on scale; each 10 dB multiplies by ten.
wrong.2: Decibels count tens of times, not the number itself.
